level: stop-fence slice 4, real remote-write Host and real loopback Agent external file effects stopped by a Windows Job; component evidence only
componentAcceptance: Win11: real remote-write, Task service/journal and a real Agent serving loopback HTTP complete four scoped synthetic file writes under a pending migration gate. Three Host acknowledgements complete, then the fourth real file and Agent succeeded receipt exist while the fixture holds the Host reply, leaving the Host attempt running and unconfirmed. After launchMigrationProcessTree().stop() returns treeStopped:true/windows-job-close and the fixture PID answers ESRCH, a 500ms window has no change in the sorted file list or SHA-256 over every filename and content, Agent operation rows, PRAGMA data_version from a pinned second connection, or heartbeat/active content and mtime. Product recover() marks the fourth attempt needs-reconciliation with HOST_INTERRUPTED/unknown and preserves possiblyApplied semantics.
productAcceptance: None. This is same-process loopback component evidence, not an independent Agent OS process, a cross-machine network, production account, machine reboot or all-domain stop-write proof. Scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12; stopWriteProvable, activationSupported and postActivationRollbackSupported remain false.
implementation: The fixture creates a real Agent with a synthetic project root, pairs and binds the real remote machine store, then drives real Task service submissions through remote-write over loopback HTTP. It does not create effect files directly.

The first three writes are acknowledged and read back. After the fourth Agent response, a deterministic fixture barrier holds the Host reply; the fourth file and Agent succeeded receipt already exist while the Host attempt remains running.

The Windows Job stop is verified independently by process death, a stable complete file fingerprint and stable Agent operation receipts/data_version for 500ms. No new file, modification or Agent commit is observed.

Cold recovery uses the product journal recover() path with a clock newer than the real service runner lease. The interrupted attempt remains unknown; the test does not turn an existing remote effect into success or rollback.
The new native suite is registered in the root npm test command.
testRuns: New suite: three consecutive standalone runs, each 1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped.
Related remote-write + executing-Task + new remote-effect suites: 18 tests / 17 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped.
Final npm test: phase one 1587/1583/0/4 and phase two 348/268/0/80; total 1935 tests, 1851 pass, 0 fail, 84 skipped.
preservedFailures: The first run used a synthetic recovery time older than the real Task service runner lease and failed with TASK_RUNNER_BUSY. Recovery now uses a fresh time after that lease.

The second run raced the short write and found no interrupted row, so recover() returned 0. A deterministic fourth-response hold now keeps the attempt running; no product assertion or implementation was weakened.
limitations: Host and Agent are in the same controlled test process and communicate only over loopback HTTP. This is not cross-machine, separate-agent-process or production deployment evidence.
The quiet window starts after the Job stop and process death observation; it is not a durable write-fence guarantee and does not cover unknown writers.
Machine reboot, other launchers/accounts, all data domains, activation and post-activation rollback remain open.
No real user profile, model inference, production process, push or release was used.
